newsitem.title: IRAQ: Aid groups leave northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Aid groups leave northern Iraq.

text.p: Aid workers headed toward the Turkish border on Tuesday from the northern Iraqi city of Arbil, captured by Iraqi troops from a Kurdish group in weekend fighting.

"International staff have been told to get out of the country as soon as possible," Jeremy Anderson, of Shelter Now International, told Reuters as he got into his truck in the town of Diyana, about two hours' drive north of Arbil on the way to the Turkish border.
"The situation is tense and our offices got looted," said Anderson, an Australian who has been in Iraq for four months.

The United States launched missile attacks on southern Iraq on Tuesday in response to President Saddam Hussein's assault on Arbil, where he ousted one Kurdish faction and installed another Kurdish group more favourable to Baghdad.
Opposition groups reported mass executions and arrests in Arbil of dissidents.

"We have left Arbil and we are monitoring the dangers to our staff hour by hour," said a worker for a leading Western aid agency. He said he cancelled plans to visit Arbil on Tuesday on the advice of his security manager.
"Agencies' relations with the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) are 'delicate' at the moment," the aid worker said.

The KDP joined with Baghdad, its erstwhile enemy, to take Arbil from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK). The PUK has reported that Iraqi troops also were on the move around Sulaimaniya, 120 km (80 miles) south of Arbil.
The aid worker said most of the scores of aid workers had already left northern Iraq or were on their way to the frontier town of Zakho to cross to Turkey.
"A handful are left in Arbil. But there is still a lot in Sulaimaniya unable to leave," he said.
